cands.name: Brent Jackson
cands.bio: Republican state senator for North Carolina Senate District 9 (District 10 before redistricting), in office since 2011. Founder, president and CEO of Jackson Farming Company in Autryville, founded 1981. Has chaired the Senate Appropriations/Base Budget and Agriculture, Energy, and Environment committees. Attended North Carolina State University.
cands.gaps: His birthplace, where he grew up and when he came to North Carolina could not be found. His campaign site has an Endorsements page, but its contents were not available, and Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him in 2024 or 2026. The bill list on his Ballotpedia page was empty. No documented actions or statements of his on data centers, development and growth, homestead property taxes, out-of-state or institutional land buyers, abortion, police pay or school choice were found. The one immigration statement is from his 2010 campaign. The gun statement is general. His campaign-site education page mentions bills he sponsored and teacher resources but gives no teacher pay figure or school-choice position. The campaign site content appears to date from around 2020.

qual.background: State senator since 2011, with about 15 years of legislative service and committee chair posts that include Appropriations/Base Budget. He has run Jackson Farming Company, a large farm business, since 1981, and earlier served on the Sampson Community College trustees and the Midway school district board.
qual.why: Long prior legislative service and years of work on budget and appropriations, plus a career as a business founder and CEO, place him in the high band. Committee chairmanships were not counted toward the score. The school and college board seats were not counted either.
qual.label: Long prior legislative service and years of work on budget and appropriations, plus a career as a business founder and CEO, place him in the high band. Committee chairmanships were not counted toward the score. The school and college board seats were not counted either.

second-amendment.evidence: His campaign site says he is a firm believer in the Second Amendment and will keep fighting for safe and responsible gun ownership. It does not name specific policies such as red-flag laws, suppressors or purchase ages.

workers-first.evidence: In his 2010 campaign site (quoted by Ballotpedia) he said he opposes amnesty for illegal immigrants and opposes taxpayer-funded welfare, medical care and higher education for them. In the same statement he supported reforming guest-worker programs such as H-2 so employers have the workers they need.
